messages:
alex: quick question — in the GET /v1/serve contract, how do routing hints interact? If the client sends:

```json
{
  "model_id": "redwood/large",
  "model_fallbacks": ["redwood/medium"],
  "routing_hints": {"region": "eu-west-1", "tier": "gold"}
}
```

Do we prefer preserving tier over region when choosing a fallback or is region precedence first? Example: preferred model only in us-west, fallback available in eu but on a lower tier.

mira: short answer: region wins for latency-critical requests. The routing policy today is region -> tier -> capacity pool. That said, it's not explicit in the public API contract/docs. We should add the precedence and an example. Also watch model-variant compatibility (kv-cache / attention config).

jonas: to expand: current implementation effectively tries matches in this order: exact region+tier, same region lower tier, other region same tier, other region lower tier. Practically: region first, then tier. That behaviour can be surprising if someone assumed tier-first. We must be explicit in the API response so callers can reason about what they got. Response should include served_region and served_tier.

sam: +1. can we add a smoke test that asserts served_model.served_region and served_model.served_tier are present on every response? I'll add runtime/tests/routing_smoke_test.py.

alex: also — clarify difference between model_hints (ordered preferences) and model_fallbacks (allowed alternates). If the client sends:

```json
{
  "model_hints": ["redwood/large", "redwood/large-quant"],
  "model_fallbacks": ["redwood/medium"]
}
```

is model_hints attempted before routing? or are they applied after region/tier resolution?

mira: they are different. model_hints are attempted first in the order they are listed — they are 'try these exact IDs before applying routing heuristics'. model_fallbacks are considered later if hints fail or are incompatible. I'll paste suggested pseudo-algo below.

```text
PSEUDO:
1) If model_hints present: attempt hints in order, honoring exact variant IDs and checking compatibility.
2) If none of hints succeed: run routing heuristic (region -> tier -> pool) to pick candidate models.
3) If candidate model not available, try model_fallbacks (in order) with same routing heuristic.
4) Return response with served_model_variant, served_region, served_tier and compatibility flags.
```

jonas: example response shape we should require (small):

```json
{
  "served_model_variant": "redwood/large-quant",
  "served_region": "eu-west-1",
  "served_tier": "silver",
  "compatibility": "kv-cache-compatible"
}
```

ci-bot: CI: PR #8462 opened by sam -> runtime/tests/routing_smoke_test.py added -> current status: 1 failing test (routing smoke). Logs: https://ci.redwood/8462/logs (CI link) :rotating_light: 

sam: on it, fixing expectation — I asserted tier-first behavior by mistake. Pushed commit fixing to expect region-first. https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8462/commits/4f1a

mira: once CI green, let's update docs: /docs/api/routing.md should include the precedence table and the example above. Also add SDK guidance: SDKs should expose a client-level routing_preference that maps to routing_hints if not provided explicitly.

alex: can someone sign off on the actual API contract text addition? I'll open a small follow-up PR to api-contracts with the paragraph and example. ping @jonas @mira for review.

jonas: will do review today. one minor nit: prefer the field name served_model_variant over served_model to be unambiguous about variant vs family id. Also add a compatibility enum (kv_cache, kv_cache_incompatible, unknown).

alex: good call. I'll update PR to use served_model_variant and add the enum. After CI green we'll do a canary deploy on dedicated/gold pool for a day and monitor latency. Thanks all :tada:
